caption:
Career cities with Ledger, Part 9, crosses South America in nine stops, and each stop shows one niche industry that city is a hub for, with a sourced fact and the jobs you could have there

So you will meet Medellin for business groups, Guayaquil for shrimp, Arequipa for alpaca fiber, Antofagasta for copper, Mendoza for wine, Montevideo for software, Hernandarias for hydropower, Manaus for electronics, and Sao Jose dos Campos for aircraft

Save the map for later, because Part 10 maps career cities across Africa

Headquartered there per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embraer (opened); only one big brand found in this city, so below the 3-logo rule

sources.claim: Medellin: GEA is a conglomerate of about 125 companies, most in Antioquia, with Bancolombia, Argos, Sura and Nutresa as main companies

Guayaquil: Ecuador shrimp exports USD 8.4 billion in 2025, up 20 percent, top export ahead of oil (Reuters via Baird Maritime). Seafoodsource gives USD 7.47 billion (CNA basis) so the figures differ by source
Guayaquil as shrimp hub: Songa headquartered in Guayaquil (search snippet only, Seafoodsource directory returned 403)
Arequipa: region is main department for alpaca fiber exports, 99 percent of sales (Peru.info, 6 Nov 2019)
Antofagasta: Cochilco says the region is the top copper area with about half of national output, share projected to fall 5 points by 2034 (Jan 2025, via Mining Reporters)
Mendoza: 74 percent of Argentine wine output, over 70 percent of planted area (Great Wine Capitals)
Mendoza: Mendoza government release says 80 percent (differs; 70 percent and 65 percent also published)
Montevideo: US buys 82 percent of Uruguay's software exports (US Commercial Service guide, undated)
Hernandarias: Itaipu generated 72,879 GWh in 2025 (La Nacion, 12 Jan 2026); location Foz do Iguacu and Hernandarias (Wikipedia Itaipu Dam)
Manaus: Polo Industrial de Manaus revenue R$ 227.67 billion in 2025 (US$ 40.90 billion), sectors electronics, IT goods, two-wheelers (Suframa)
Manaus: R$ 227.6 billion in 2025, up 11.02 percent; 131,401 direct jobs average (Portal Amazonia)
Sao Jose dos Campos: Embraer delivered 244 aircraft in 2025 versus 206 in 2024 (Aviacion al Dia); headquarters Sao Jose dos Campos (Wikipedia Embraer)
Embraer 233 deliveries (commercial and executive only; 244 includes 11 defence aircraft) (ch-aviation)

Logos: Grupo Sura headquartered in Medellin

openQuestions: Slot: Part 9 Fri 4 Dec 18:00 VN is a proposal; Part 8 (Asia) must name Part 9 South America.
Word count is below the 250-285 in the task because Part 5 used 242 words for 110.9 s; 285 words would run about 130 s and break the 2-minute cap. Hoang to confirm that cap wins.

Only 3 logos in the city scene are met for Medellin (Nutresa, Argos, Sura). Sao Jose dos Campos has one (Embraer). Other stops show no logos. Logo files must be obtained by the lead, none downloaded here.
Hernandarias is a small town; Itaipu is binational (Brazil and Paraguay), so keep the wording neutral and show only the Paraguay flag at this stop. Alternatively use Foz do Iguacu or Ciudad del Este.

Weak: Arequipa's 99 percent is a 2019 figure; Montevideo's 82 percent is undated and national; Mendoza share varies by source (65 to 80 percent); Guayaquil shrimp figure is national (USD 8.4 billion Reuters vs USD 7.47 billion CNA) and the Guayaquil hub claim rests on a snippet; Antofagasta share is a Cochilco projection from Jan 2025.

Two Brazil stops (Manaus and Sao Jose dos Campos). Swap one for a new country (for example Santa Cruz in Bolivia or Georgetown in Guyana) if Hoang wants maximum variety; I left Guyana and Venezuela out because of the border dispute.
Jobs lines are examples of roles that exist in such industries, not sourced vacancies; they sit on screen as chips, not in the voice.

Sweep 18 Nov 2026 (rule from Hoang's Part 6 and 7 notes: open on the region's main finance hub; big business, commodity and energy hubs before niche or creative picks): Part 9 opens on Medellin business groups and has no Sao Paulo, South America's biggest finance hub (B3 exchange, the big banks). Proposal: open on Sao Paulo for finance; consider an oil and gas stop (Rio de Janeiro offshore oil, or Neuquen's Vaca Muerta) in place of a niche pick; Antofagasta copper already fits
